title: Fourth Word Comparison On The Necessity Of The Prescribed Prayers

questions.question: In the story, what did the ruler give to each servant at the start?
questions.answer: He gave each one twenty-four gold coins.

questions.question: Where did the ruler send the two servants?
questions.answer: He sent them to live on one of his rich farms.

questions.question: About how far away was that place?
questions.answer: It was about two months away.

questions.question: What were the servants told to do with the money?
questions.answer: They were told to use it for travel and for things needed for their home there.

questions.question: How far from the farm was the station?
questions.answer: It was one day away.

questions.question: Name one kind of travel they could use on the way.
questions.answer: They could use the railway.

questions.question: What did the careful servant do with some of his money on the way?
questions.answer: He spent a little of it in a good way and gained much more.

questions.question: What happened to the careful servant’s money after that good use?
questions.answer: It grew many, many times.

questions.question: What did the careless servant do with most of his money?
questions.answer: He wasted it on games and fun.

questions.question: After wasting his money, how many gold coins did he still have?
questions.answer: He had one left.

questions.question: What did his friend tell him to buy with that last coin?
questions.answer: A ticket.

questions.question: Why was buying the ticket important?
questions.answer: It would help him avoid a hard, hungry walk.

questions.question: What long, hard place would he have to cross without the ticket?
questions.answer: A desert.

questions.question: How long would that walk take?
questions.answer: Two months.

questions.question: What did the friend say the master might do if he used the last coin wisely?
questions.answer: The master might forgive him and even let him ride on a plane.

questions.question: How fast could they reach their new home in that case?
questions.answer: In one day.

questions.question: What does the story teach about the servant who refuses to buy the ticket?
questions.answer: He is making a foolish and harmful choice.

questions.question: Why is spending the last coin on bad fun a poor choice?
questions.answer: Because it gives short fun but makes him lose a much greater good.

questions.question: How many servants are in the story?
questions.answer: Two servants.

questions.question: Who sent them on the journey?
questions.answer: A powerful ruler.

questions.question: What kind of place were they going to?
questions.answer: A rich royal farm.

questions.question: What did the ruler command them to buy first for the trip?
questions.answer: Their tickets.

questions.question: What else did the ruler tell them to buy?
questions.answer: Things needed for their house there.

questions.question: What does the station’s distance show about the trip to the farm?
questions.answer: It shows the station was much closer than the farm.

questions.question: Could they all travel in only one way?
questions.answer: No, there were many ways to travel.

questions.question: What decided which travel they could use?
questions.answer: How much money they had.

questions.question: Which servant acted wisely with his money?
questions.answer: The fortunate servant.

questions.question: How do we know he acted wisely?
questions.answer: He spent only a little and it brought a huge gain.

questions.question: Which servant acted without thinking?
questions.answer: The lazy, unlucky servant.

questions.question: What kind of things did he choose instead of what he needed?
questions.answer: He chose useless fun and gambling.

questions.question: What advice did the friend give him about the last coin?
questions.answer: Use it for a ticket.

questions.question: What two problems would happen if he did not buy the ticket?
questions.answer: He would have to walk far and go hungry.

questions.question: What does the friend’s advice show about the master?
questions.answer: The master is generous and may show mercy.

questions.question: What might the master give him besides forgiveness?
questions.answer: A ride on an airplane.

questions.question: Why is the last coin compared to a key?
questions.answer: Because it could open the way to something much better.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the story?
questions.answer: A small wise choice can bring a big good, but wasting it brings trouble.

questions.question: What is said about the prescribed prayers at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: They are called the support of religion.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the cost of gaining prayer’s benefit?
questions.answer: It says the cost is very small.

questions.question: What does the story help us understand about leaving the prayers?
questions.answer: It helps us see that neglecting them is foolish and harmful.

questions.question: How much money did each servant receive?
questions.answer: Twenty-four gold pieces.

questions.question: For what future place were they preparing?
questions.answer: A place where they would settle and live.

questions.question: What did the ruler say was available for travel?
questions.answer: Different kinds of transportation were available.

questions.question: Which servant used part of his money in a beneficial way?
questions.answer: The fortunate servant did.

questions.question: How good was the result of his spending?
questions.answer: It brought a very great increase.

questions.question: What kind of person was the other servant described as?
questions.answer: He was lazy and unfortunate.

questions.question: How did he lose nearly all his money?
questions.answer: He threw it away on bad entertainment and gambling.

questions.question: What was left after that?
questions.answer: Only one gold coin.

questions.question: What did his friend want him to do right away?
questions.answer: Spend that last coin on travel.

questions.question: What might save him from crossing the desert on foot?
questions.answer: Buying the ticket might save him.

questions.question: What feeling is the reader meant to have about refusing to buy the ticket?
questions.answer: The reader should see it as very silly and damaging.

questions.question: Why is the pleasure he chose called passing?
questions.answer: Because it lasts only a short time.

questions.question: What is better in the story: short fun or using money for the journey?
questions.answer: Using the money for the journey is better.

questions.question: What can we infer about the wise servant’s thinking?
questions.answer: He cared about the goal and planned ahead.

questions.question: What can we infer about the foolish servant’s thinking?
questions.answer: He cared more about quick fun than his real need.

questions.question: What kind of story is used to explain the lesson?
questions.answer: A comparison story.

questions.question: How certain does the passage say this lesson is?
questions.answer: It says it is as clear as simple math.

questions.question: What was special about the ruler’s farm?
questions.answer: It was rich and royal.

questions.question: Why were the servants given money before the trip?
questions.answer: So they could travel and prepare for living there.

questions.question: What was one place they needed to reach first?
questions.answer: The station.

questions.question: What was one fast way of travel named in the story?
questions.answer: An airplane.

questions.question: What happened because one servant spent carefully?
questions.answer: His small spending brought great profit.

questions.question: How much did the careless servant spend badly?
questions.answer: He wasted twenty-three gold coins.

questions.question: What do gambling and amusements show about his choices?
questions.answer: They show he chose fun instead of wisdom.

questions.question: Who tried to help the careless servant?
questions.answer: His friend did.

questions.question: What warning did the friend give about the trip without a ticket?
questions.answer: It would be a long, lonely, hungry journey.

questions.question: What kind of land would he need to cross?
questions.answer: A desert.

questions.question: What hope did the friend give about the master?
questions.answer: The master might pardon him and help him.

questions.question: If he got extra help, how much shorter could the trip become?
questions.answer: It could become one day instead of two months.

questions.question: Why is the servant’s stubborn refusal such a bad idea?
questions.answer: Because he throws away a great chance for a tiny pleasure.

questions.question: What does this story teach about using even a small amount wisely?
questions.answer: Even a little can lead to something very valuable.

questions.question: Which servant shows good judgment?
questions.answer: The one who thinks ahead and spends carefully.

questions.question: Which servant shows bad judgment?
questions.answer: The one who wastes almost everything and ignores good advice.

questions.question: What did the ruler call the farm the servants were going to?
questions.answer: He described it as one of his rich royal farms.

questions.question: How long was the full trip to that place?
questions.answer: Two months.

questions.question: What did the ruler tell them to do before reaching the farm?
questions.answer: He told them to get what they needed on the way.

questions.question: Did the ruler leave them with no way to travel?
questions.answer: No, he provided many travel options.

questions.question: Which servant’s actions pleased the master?
questions.answer: The fortunate servant’s actions pleased him.

questions.question: How can we tell the master was pleased?
questions.answer: The servant’s good use of money brought a huge return.

questions.question: What word best describes the second servant’s spending: careful or wasteful?
questions.answer: Wasteful.

questions.question: What was the second servant’s friend trying to protect him from?
questions.answer: From a long, hard, hungry trip.

questions.question: Why was the final gold coin so important?
questions.answer: It was enough to help him continue the journey the right way.

questions.question: What might happen if the master showed mercy?
questions.answer: He might forgive the servant and give extra help.

questions.question: What does the airplane in the story suggest about the journey?
questions.answer: It suggests the journey could become much easier and faster.

questions.question: What does the desert suggest about going the wrong way?
questions.answer: It suggests hardship and suffering.

questions.question: Was the friend giving bad advice or good advice?
questions.answer: He was giving good advice.

questions.question: How should a smart person view the servant’s refusal to buy a ticket?
questions.answer: As a very foolish choice.

questions.question: What is the difference between the two servants in one short idea?
questions.answer: One plans wisely, and the other wastes foolishly.

questions.question: What comes from the wise servant’s small sacrifice?
questions.answer: A very large benefit.

questions.question: What comes from the foolish servant’s search for fun?
questions.answer: Loss and trouble.

questions.question: At the start, what did both servants have equally?
questions.answer: They both had the same amount of gold.

questions.question: What does that show before they make choices?
questions.answer: It shows they began with the same chance.

questions.question: What changed their futures in the story?
questions.answer: The choices they made with their money.

questions.question: What was the first servant like in his spending?
questions.answer: He was careful and wise.

questions.question: What was the second servant like in his spending?
questions.answer: He was careless and lazy.

questions.question: What did the first servant gain from a small expense?
questions.answer: He gained a huge increase.

questions.question: What did the second servant gain from wasting his money?
questions.answer: He gained almost nothing and was left in trouble.

questions.question: How much money was enough to still help him if used well?
questions.answer: One gold coin.

questions.question: What important thing could that one coin buy?
questions.answer: A ticket.

questions.question: Why did the friend speak to him so strongly?
questions.answer: Because the servant was in danger of making a terrible choice.

questions.question: What hard things are named together to show the trouble ahead?
questions.answer: Walking, hunger, and crossing a desert.

questions.question: What does the friend believe about the master’s character?
questions.answer: He believes the master is kind and generous.

questions.question: What two good things might the servant receive from the master?
questions.answer: Forgiveness and a ride on a plane.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the ticket and something valuable?
questions.answer: It is compared to something that opens a treasure.

questions.question: Why is wasting the last coin worse than it first seems?
questions.answer: Because losing that small coin means losing a much greater reward.

questions.question: What does the passage want us to think about stubbornness?
questions.answer: Stubbornness can make a person choose harm over good.

questions.question: Which is more important in the story: the short pleasure or the long-term good?
questions.answer: The long-term good is more important.

questions.question: What is the main message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Prayer is very valuable, and neglecting it is a harmful mistake.
